subject: Dedicated capacity: sizing notes, pick of GPU mix & ops next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — dedicated path & immediate sizing asks

Thanks again for a productive call today, Elena — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of what I heard you say:
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) given throughput predictability and data isolation needs; still evaluating VPC option for tighter controls.
- Traffic profile (rough): peak ~180 req/s, steady-state ~55–70 req/s. Average response ~420 tokens; token mix skews medium (64–512) with ~25% longer sessions (512–2k).
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 600ms, target median <200ms for short requests.
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress; need to confirm retention/audit log requirements for the Dedicated/private path.

Immediate asks I promised to surface internally:
1) Recommended GPU mix for an initial dedicated pool that balances cost + latency for your token mix and concurrency.
2) Ops assumptions: warmup/KV cache sizing, expected concurrency per model shard, and runbook for burst handling.
3) Next meeting: technical deep-dive with our infra/ops engineer and your platform lead to agree on bench targets and VPC checklist.

Attached: a short CSV you mentioned (traffic_profile.csv) and your security questionnaire (sec_qs.pdf). I'll circulate a first-pass capacity worksheet by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marissa to provide an initial GPU-mix recommendation + cost ballpark (internal deliverable).
- Schedule 60-min deep-dive week of June 1 (tech + security).
- You to confirm whether you want a Hosted fallback lane for short-term during ramp.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the worksheet link.

— Karthik

From: Elena Morales <elena@clearpath.ai>

Date: 2027-05-29T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated path & immediate sizing asks

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick recap. Confirming a few details and adding context for sizing:

- The CSV I uploaded is our minute-level sampled requests over the last 30 days. Peak minute in sample ~10,500 requests -> ~175 req/s (matches our call).
- Average request payload: ~120 tokens in prompt, average completion ~300 tokens (so your 420 avg is accurate for end-to-end).
- Concurrency characteristics: most clients are bursty; 80% of sessions complete within 2–3s, but heavy inference (multi-turn summarization) stretches to 20–30s occasionally.
- Compliance: we require customer-data separation and that logs for customer X are retained 12 months. VPC is preferred but we can discuss whether Dedicated + strict IAM satisfies the immediate needs.

Two asks from our side before the tech call:
1) Please include a conservative and an aggressive sizing scenario (cost delta between them).
2) Can you confirm if we can route a small % of traffic to Hosted as a fallback during incidents?

Attached the security questions (sec_qs.pdf) and I've shared the Drive folder to your team.

— Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform, ClearPath AI
elena@clearpath.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@clearpath.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap — initial dedicated sizing scenarios (conservative / aggressive)

Hi Elena — thanks for the data. I pulled the CSV and sketched two scenarios in the attached capacity_worksheet.xlsx. High-level notes below.

Quick assumptions we used (please tell me if any are off):- Model: open-encoder-70b (your current preference) at FP16 w/ 4-bit quantized variants for lower-cost lanes.- Median prompt+completion tokens: 420 (as confirmed).- Target SLO: P95 <= 600ms for medium requests, P95 <= 1.2s for long sessions.

Conservative (cost-focused, higher concurrency per-GPU):- Baseline pool: 12 x A10G (or equivalently A100-80GB) configured with dynamic batching + quantized runtime.- Expected sustained capacity: ~60–80 req/s with median latency target met; handles steady-state + modest bursts via prewarming.- Warm KV cache strategy (prefix caching) to reduce work for repeated user sessions.

Aggressive (latency-focused, faster tail):- Baseline pool: 6 x H100 + 8 x A10G. Route long-context jobs to H100s (better throughput for 2k tokens) and short/medium to A10G.- Expected sustained capacity: ~180 req/s with headroom for 20% bursts; P95 latency improves ~30–40% on medium requests.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:- Hybrid pool requires smart routing; we can gate by request length and estimated tokens-out. That adds small routing latency but materially reduces cost vs all-H100.- KV cache sizing: for your 25% long sessions we recommend 200–300GB of cached KV to avoid repeated recompute for multi-turn flows.- Canary/fallback: yes — we support routing a configurable percent of traffic to Hosted as a fallback lane and automatic failover rules (we'll capture this in the runbook).

Attachments: capacity_worksheet.xlsx (two tabs: conservative / aggressive with cost model and recommended autoscale policies).

Next steps I propose:
1) 60-min technical deep-dive (include our infra eng and your platform lead) — proposed slots: June 1 10:00am PT or June 2 2:00pm PT.
2) We'll populate the Drive checklist for VPC onboarding and request SOC2 evidence mapping.
3) Karthik to surface commercial delta for the two scenarios (inc. one-off reserved pricing for Dedicated).

If that all looks good I'll lock the June 1 slot.

— Marissa

- I'll also send a short note to our security team to pre-populate responses for sec_qs.pdf so you have initial evidence before the deep-dive.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/CLP-2027-195 (I've added notes and the worksheet link).
